target.name: Unlimited Industries
target.founder: Alex Modon, Jordan Stern, Tara Viswanathan

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $12M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Unlimited Industries is a seed-stage housing and construction company founded by Alex Modon, Jordan Stern, and Tara Viswanathan, having raised $12M to date. The relevant comp universe consists of five private peers in construction technology and automation: BotBuilt, Apis Cor, Ground Control Development, ADMARES, and Hedral. No directly comparable public companies trade in this subsector.

The stage-progression method serves as the primary valuation anchor. Using the $12M total raised as a proxy for current value, application of a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $30M. This approach assumes the company will achieve the operational and financial metrics necessary to command such a multiple at subsequent fundraising.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $26M to $34M, with a median of $30M. The narrow range reflects reliance on a single applicable method; triangulation depth is constrained by limited public comparables and sparse disclosed valuations among private peers. Key uncertainties include the precise burn rate and path to Series A metrics, the competitive positioning relative to the named peer set, and market conditions affecting construction technology fundraising. Further diligence on unit economics and customer traction would strengthen conviction in this range.
